ai.title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.14005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. How can we then evaluate machines that may become more capable than the current machines and the people who write the tests? One answer to the question hinges on inverse problems, inductive inference questions for which difficulty depends on the complexity of the underlying mechanism, given the observations and the previous knowledge. Levin's Kt, a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity, puts a theoretical upper bound to that difficulty, balancing the simplest representation encoding for the mechanism and the logarithm of the time steps to run that mechanism. Previous tests derived from Levin's Kt, such as the original C-test, are based on minimalistic Universal Turing Machines (UTM), capable of very limited representations and no previous knowledge. Reasoning large language models (LLM) are UTMs that capture a compendium of human culture as knowledge, using prompts as natural language programs. This paper presents the first test based on Levin's Kt with LLMs as representational machines. Fresh test items can be produced at high difficulties, estimated in a ratio scale measured in bits, before any human or frontier model can solve them. ai.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.

ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.14970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs), there is an increasing demand for effective personalization techniques that can adapt model behavior to individual user preferences. Existing approaches rely primarily on in-context personalization, parametric adaptation, or personalized reward modeling, but respectively incur recurring costs in context management, model optimization and deployment, or multi-candidate generation and scoring. These limitations become particularly restrictive when user observations are sparse and the preference evidence relevant to each query varies across contexts and over time. To address these challenges, we propose \modelname, a fine-grained and instance-tailored steering framework that dynamically generates sample-level interference vectors from user data and injects them into the model's forward pass for personalized adaptation. ai.title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.15029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated disease classification from patient-reported symptoms requires balancing the speed of lightweight discriminative models against the contextual understanding and latency costs of autoregressive large language models (LLMs). Decision foundation models offer an alternative by mapping representations directly to candidate classes without free-form text generation. We adapt Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark. Using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) with differential learning rates and a stratified split of 960 training and 240 test cases, the model achieves 95.42% diagnostic accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.9551. This improves upon the reported zero-shot baselines of 61.67% for a remote API and 65.00% for a local unadapted initialization, and outperforms the ClinicalBERT baseline (90.90%). By evaluating candidate logits in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding, inference takes under 80 milliseconds per record on a single GPU, yielding a reported 31-fold speedup over generative LLM baselines. To examine symptom-level evidence, we introduce a Leave-One-Symptom-Out (LOSO) counterfactual perturbation framework. ai.title: Do LLMs differentiate linguistic traits internally?: A layer-wise analysis
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.15203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models often produce judgments that resemble human responses, but it remains unclear whether they internally capture linguistic nuances such as conventional versus idiomatic meaning. A layer-wise representational analysis was conducted on two equal-sized pre-trained models, Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma-3-1B-PT, to examine whether and where these models differentiate linguistic traits from input. The analysis combined layer-wise probing with geometric distance measures, using the top embedding dimensions ranked by principal component loadings for each layer. The results show that even with equal capacity, models organize linguistic information in fundamentally different ways, suggesting the need to analyze internal representational geometry, examining not just behavioral outputs but semantic space alignment when evaluating how closely human and model language interpretation correspond.

ai.title: Feedback as an Interface: Controlling Form and Detail in LLM Translation Refinement
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.15661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback presentation shapes how LLMs use evaluator judgments during translation refinement. We introduce a machine translation protocol that keeps the evaluator score, main issue, and recommendation fixed while varying feedback form and supporting detail. Across seven models and six translation directions, low-load feedback outperforms high-load feedback in all 42 translator-direction settings under xCOMET. On the 29,400-record rewriting subset, mean xCOMET scores multiplied by 100 are 83.30 for low-load feedback and 80.67 for high-load feedback; the full-matrix original-translation reference mean is 83.46. MetricX-24 supports the low-load advantage on a stratified subset. A no-feedback second pass yields a small improvement over the original translations, and direct evaluator prompting reproduces the low-load advantage without a separate rewriting stage. These results show that compact feedback limits the quality loss from evaluator-guided refinement in the evaluated high-resource MT settings.
ai.summary: Feedback presentation shapes how LLMs use evaluator judgments during translation refinement.

Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will attend the meeting. ai.title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases. The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. HUD largely achieved workforce reductions through deferred resignation programs. Over half the employees who separated had at least 10 years of service at HUD, including 41 percent with more than 20 years of service. HUD did not publish notice of any reorganization plans that led to field office closures in 2025, though in 2026 it announced plans to consolidate one field office into a nearby regional office. ai.title: Federal Law Enforcement: CBP and ICE Should Improve Body-Worn Camera Program Management
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Body-worn cameras provide law enforcement personnel with the capability to record interactions with the public. When initiating their body-worn camera programs, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) each developed a plan that included key components of a comprehensive program management plan. However, CBP and ICE have not updated their program plans since 2022 and 2024, respectively. They have therefore not taken into account significant changes in the program, such as increases in the number of cameras scheduled for deployment and a 2025 pause in further camera deployment. Body-Worn Camera and Functional Buttons CBP and ICE have stated desired results for their programs, including enhancing officer safety, transparency, accountability, and public trust. Although CBP and ICE implemented some measures to track information about camera availability and reliability, they have not implemented results-oriented performance goals and measures. Doing so would help them assess the results of their body-worn camera programs. For example, potential goals and measures might involve use of footage in use of force investigations. CBP and ICE have established policies related to camera use and the management of footage and implemented related oversight mechanisms to help ensure compliance with policy. trade.title: 經濟部貿易救濟審議會就越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品反傾銷案初步認定國內產業遭受實質損害
trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.via: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（12）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品反傾銷案之產業損害初步調查結果進行審議，認定有合理跡象顯示國內產業遭受實質損害。後續將移請財政部進行傾銷調查。 經濟部表示，本案調查資料涵蓋期間（112年1月至115年6月），越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品進口量自113年至114年大幅增加，進口價格逐年下降，且皆低於國產品內銷價格。國產品為與之競爭不得不跟進減價，減價幅度更甚於涉案貨物，惟因內銷價格仍高於涉案傾銷貨物致流失客戶，即便我國需求有所成長時也不見改善，導致市場占有率持續下降及內銷虧損擴大，國內產業營運狀況持續惡化；至115年1-6月因申請人宣布即將申請反傾銷調查，加上價差縮小，國內產業各項經濟指標，包括內銷虧損情形始不致繼續惡化。顯示越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品傾銷進口對國內產業造成不利影響。 依據「平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法」規定，我國反傾銷案件調查由財政部與經濟部分工，分別負責「傾銷」調查與「損害」調查。程序上先由經濟部進行產業損害初步調查，如認定成立，則移請財政部進行傾銷「初步」及「最後」調查，如其「最後」調查認定傾銷成立，再由經濟部進行產業損害「最後」調查，最終交由財政部決定是否課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部將產業損害初步調查認定結果通知財政部後，財政部應於通知送達之翌日起70日內作成有無傾銷的初步認定，並決定是否臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部表示，本案如須進行產業損害「最後」調查，經濟部將就國內產業狀況進一步瞭解及查證，並蒐集各方針對課徵反傾銷稅對下游產業等國家整體經濟利益影響之意見，提供財政部關稅稅率審議小組參考。屆時並不排除其他任何新增不同事實與分析，而獲致不同的結論。 有關產業損害初步調查報告公開版可於今(115)年11月12日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.raw_summary: 財政部 公告 發文日期：中華民國115年10月13日 發文字號：台財關字第1151027218號 附件： 主旨：力麟科技股份有限公司申請對自中國大陸產製進口特定聚醯胺薄膜課徵反傾銷稅、臨時課徵反傾銷稅及回溯課徵反傾銷稅案，經本部初步認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，自115年10月19日起臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 依據：平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法（下稱實施辦法）第12條至第14條，及本部關稅稅率審議小組115年9月24日第72次會議決議。 公告事項： 一、本部關稅稅率審議小組第72次會議決議略以：本案依據經濟部產業損害初步調查結果，認定有合理跡象顯示，涉案傾銷進口產品對國內產業造成實質損害，且我國產業在調查期間將繼續遭受損害；復經本部初步調查認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，爰依實施辦法第13條規定，對相關涉案廠商之涉案產品臨時課徵反傾銷稅，為期4個月。 二、本案臨時課徵反傾銷稅之範圍、對象、稅率及期間如下： (一)課徵範圍： １、貨品名稱：特定聚醯胺薄膜（Certain Polyamide Film）。 ２、貨品範圍：以重量計含超過50%之聚醯胺-6，不論其表面是否經印刷、塗覆以任何材料或進行任何表面處理，未切或已切成長方形，但未經進一步加工之薄膜或箔。 ３、貨品規格： (１)厚度：0.0114公厘（含）以上至0.0315公厘（含）以下。 (２)寬度：超過5公厘。 (３)排除項目：具下列任一成分或特性之薄膜，不屬涉案貨物： 甲、薄膜表面含有金屬成分者。 乙、攝氏20度至23度且相對溼度50%至65%之測試條件下，薄膜厚度為0.015公厘時，氧氣穿透率小於15mL/(m?·day·atm)，即小於15毫升/(每平方公尺·每日·1標準大氣壓的純氧)者。 ４、參考貨品分類號列：39209229105及39209229203。 ５、用途：應用於食品、化學用品、醫療（藥）用品與電子材料包裝等。 (二)課徵對象： １、輸出國或產製國：中國大陸。 ２、國外製造商及出口商：昆山運城塑業有限公司、運城其龍新材料有限公司、鶴山運城新材料有限公司、廈門長塑實業有限公司、福建長塑實業有限公司、滄州東鴻制膜科技有限公司、滄州東鴻包裝材料有限公司、重慶明珠塑料有限公司、德州東鴻新材料有限公司、蕪湖明珠制膜科技有限公司、曉星化纖（嘉興）有限公司及佛山佛塑科技集團股份有限公司。 ３、國內進口商：慕明企業有限公司、展仝企業有限公司、建?股份有限公司及光展應材股份有限公司。 ４、其他未列名之涉案貨物製造商、出口商或進口商。 (三)臨時課徵稅率： １、昆山運城塑業有限公司（製造商）、運城其龍新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）及鶴山運城新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）：0%。 ２、其他製造商或出口商：40.21%。 ３、前揭個別廠商之臨時課徵稅率，係依其於調查期間提供資料計算決定，故涉案貨物須由該等廠商於該國生產製造並直接出口至我國，始得適用。 (四)課徵期間：依據實施辦法第13條第3項規定，臨時課徵之反傾銷稅，其課徵期間最長為4個月；如經占涉案貿易額相當比例之國外出口商請求，得延長為6個月。 三、本案尚須進行傾銷最後調查，依實地查核結果或其他新事證，可能獲致不同之傾銷差率或作成不同結論。 四、本案後續調查程序：依據實施辦法第14條及第16條規定，本部初步認定之案件，應於初步認定公告之翌日起60日內完成有無傾銷之最後認定。經最後認定有傾銷事實者，本部應即通知經濟部。經濟部應於接獲通知之翌日起40日內，作成該傾銷是否損害我國產業之最後調查認定並通知本部。本部應於接獲經濟部通知之翌日起10日內，提交關稅稅率審議小
